newsitem.title: BELGIUM: The euro, the EU's great leveller says Belgium.
newsitem.headline: The euro, the EU's great leveller says Belgium.

text.p: Belgium on Thursday launched a publicity campaign to persuade consumers and small businesses of the benefits of switching to Europe's single currency, the euro.

It promises Belgians that when the euro hits the streets in 2002 they will be able to move from sipping a glass of beer in Amsterdam to licking ice on the Cote d'Azur without changing the cash in their pockets.

The campaign is geared to the launch of the euro for business and banks on January 1, 1999. It includes 1.5 million glossy brochures at post offices and a series of advertisements on radio, television and in newspapers, and is aimed primarily at the general public and small businesses.

The brochure explains the criteria for countries joining the euro and sets out some of the benefits for individuals such as not having to change currency when travelling, and being able to directly compare prices of the same products in other countries.

It also publicises the Belgian government's euro internet site. http://euro.fgov.be and a series of e-mail addresses and telephone information lines for people wanting to get deeper into the mysteries of the coming currency.
